title: Yeimar bar Chasho
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Ketubot 84b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.84b) relates that he was owed money by a certain man who died and left a boat. Yeimar bar Chasho went and told his agent to seize the boat in payment of his debt. Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua met him (the agent) and told him that he had not acquired it, because he was seizing property on behalf of one creditor to the detriment of others.[^1]

notes.text: The parenthesis “the agent” belongs to the person whom the sages met, not to the sages themselves. The exact boat-and-agent narrative in Ketubot 84b, William Davidson Edition — Vocalized Aramaic, explicitly reads רב פפא ורב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, supporting “Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua” in this occurrence. The passage continues at 85a:1. This is title evidence for the cited chain, not an authority identity assignment. בע״ח means a creditor.
